a: सीमा — 1 Boundary, limit, border, margin, frontier. --2 A mound or ridge serving to mark the boundary of a field, village &c.; सीमां प्रति समुत्पन्ने विवादे Ms. 8. 245; Y. 2. 152. --3 A mark, land-mark. --4 A bank, shore, coast. --5 The horizon. --6 A suture (as of a skull). --7 The bounds of morality or decorum, limits of propriety. --8 The highest or utmost limit, highest point, climax; सीमेव पद्मासनकौशलस्थ Bk. 1. 6. --9 A field. --10 The nape of the neck. --11 The scrotum. --Comp. --अधिपः a neighbouring prince. --अंतः {1} a boundary-line, border, frontier-line. {2} the utmost limit. ˚पूजनं {1} the ceremony of worshipping or honouring a village-boundary. {2} worshipping the bridegroom when he arrives at the village-boundary. --उल्लंघनं transgressing or leaping over a boundary, crossing a frontier (now performed on the Daśarā day). --निश्चयः a legal decision with respect to land-marks or boundaries. --लिंगं a boundary-mark, land-mark. --वादः a dispute about boundaries. --विनिर्णयः settlement of disputed boundary-questions. --विवादः litigation about boundaries. ˚धर्मः the law regarding disputes about boundaries. --वृक्षः a tree serving as a boundary-mark. --संधिः the meeting of two boundaries.

salilavatI matsyaSabdasya svaDArajalalakzaRatvAt । nEDAnI niKAtatuzANgArAdimatI । tezAM niKAtatvena niDAnatulyatvAt । BayavarjitA arTipratyarTiparasparasampratipattinirmmitA । rAjaSAsananItA । jYAtfcihnABAve rAjecCayA nirmmitA evamBUtAyAM zoQA vivAdaH saMBavati । yaTAha kAtyAyanaH । “ADikyaM nyUnatA cAMSe astinAstitvameva ca aBogaBuktiH sImA ca zaqBUvAdasya hetavaH ॥” iti । taTA hi । mamAtra paYcanivarttanAyA BUmeraDikA BUrastIti kenacidukte paYcanivarttanEva nADiketyADikye vivAdaH । paYcanivarttanA madIyAM BUrityuktena tato nyUnEveti nyUnatAyAm । paYcanivarttano mamAMSa ityukte'MSa eva nAstItyastinAstitvavivAdaH samBavati । madIyA BUH prAgavidyamAnaBogEva Bujyata ityuktena santatA cirantanyeva me BuktirityaBogaBuktO vivAdaH । iyaM maryyAdeyaYceti sImAvivAda iti zawprakAra eva vivAdaH samBavati । zawprakAre'pi BUvivAde SrutyarTAByAM sImAyA api nirRIyamAnatvAt sImAnirRayaprakaraRe tasyAntarBAvaH । samantAdBavAH sAmantAH । catasfzu dikzvanantarA grAmAdayasta ca pratisImaM vyavasTitAH । “grAmo grAmezu sAmantaH kzetraM kzetrasya kIrttitam । gfhaM gfhasya nirddizwaM samantAt pariraBya hi ॥” iti kAtyAyanavacanAt । grAmAdiSabdena tatsTAH puruzA lakzyanta । grAmaH palAyata iti yaTA । sAmantagrahaRaYca tatsaMsaktAdyupalakzaRArTam । uktaYca kAtyAyanena । “saMsaktakAstu sAmantAstatsaMsaktAstaTottarAH । saMsaktasaktasaMsaktAH padmAkArAH prakIrttitAH ॥” iti । sTavirA vfdDAH । AdigrahaRena mOlodDatayorgra haRam । vfdDAdilakzaRaYca tenEvoktam । “nizpAdyamAnaM yErdfzwaM tat kAryyaM tadguRAnvitEH । vfdDA vA yadi vAvfdDAste ca vfdDAH prakIttitAH ॥ ye tatra pUrvvaM sAmantAH paScAddeSAntaraM gatAH । tanmUlatvAttu te mOlA fziBiH parikIrttitAH ॥ upaSra vaRasamBogakAryyAKyAnopacihnitAH । udDaranti punaryasmAdudDatAste tataH smftAH ॥” gopA gocArakAH । “sImAkfzARAH sImAsaMnihitakzetrakarzakAH .” sarvve ca vanagocarA vanacAriRo vyADAdayaste ca manunoktAH । “vyADAn SAkunikAn gopAn kEvarttAn mUlaKAtakAn । vyAlagrAhAnuYCavfttInanyAMSca vanagocarAn ॥” svalamunnato BUpradeSaH । aNgAro'gne rucCizwam । tuzA DAnyatvacaH । drumA nyagroDAdayaH । seturjalapravAhabanDaH । cEtyaM pAzARAdibanDaH । AdyaSabdena veRuvAlukAdInAM grahaRam । etAni ca prakASAprakASaBedena dviHprakArARi । taTA ca manuH । “sImAvfkzAMstu kurvvIta nyagroDASvatTakiMSukAn SAlmalIn SAlatAlAMSca kzIriRaScEva pAdapAn ॥ gulmAn veRUMSca viviDAn SamI vallI sTalAni ca । SarAn kubjakagulmAMSca taTA sImA na naSyati ॥ taqAgAnudapAnAni vApyaH prasravaRAni ca । somAsanDizu kAryyARi devatAyatanAni ca ॥” iti prakASarUpARi ॥ “upacCannAni cAnyAni sImAliNgAni kArayet । sImAjYAne nfRAM vIkzyanityaM loke viparyyayam ॥ aSmano'syIni gobAlAMstuzAna BasmakapAlikAH । karIzamizwakANgAraSarkarAvAlukAstaTA ॥ yAni cEvaM prakArARi kAlAdBUmirna Bakzayet । tAni sanDizu somAyA aprakASAni kArayet ॥ etErliNgErnayet sImAM rAjA vivadamAnayoH ॥” pracCannaliNgAni etEH prakASAprakASarUpErliNgEH sAmantAdipradarSitEH somAM prati vivadamAnayoH sImAnirRayaM kuryyAdrAjA ॥ * ॥ yadA punaScihnAni na santi vidyamAnAni vA liNgAliNgatayA sandigDAni tadA nirRayopAyamAha । “sAmantA vA samagrAmAScatvAro'zwO daSApi vA raktasragvasanAH sImAM nayeyuH kzitiDAriRaH ॥” sAmantAH pUrvvoktalakzaRAH । samagrAmAScatvAro'zwO daSApi vA ityevaM samasaMKyAH pratyAsannagrAmIRAH । raktasragviRo raktAmbaraDarAH mUrdDAropitakzitiKaRqAH sImAnaM nayeyuH pradarSayeyuH sAmantA veti vikalpABiDAnaM smftyuttaroktasAkzyaBiprAyam । yaTAha manuH । “sAkzipratyaya eva syAt sImAvAdavinirRayaH .” tatra ca sAkziRAM nirRetftvaM muKyaM tadaBAve sAmantAnAm । taduktam । “sAkzyaBAve tu catvAro grAmAH sImantavAsinaH sImAviniRayaM kuryyuH prayatA rAjasanniDO ॥” tadaBAve tatsaMsaktAdInAM nirRetftvam । yaTAha kAtyAyanaH । “svArTasidDO praduzwezu sAmante zvarTagOravAt । tatsaMsaktEstu kattavya udDAro nAtra saMSayaH ॥ saMsaktasaktadAze tu tatsaMsaktAH prakIrttitAH । karttavyA na praduzwAstu rAjYA DarmmaM vijAnatA ॥” sAmantAdyaBAve mOlAdayo grAhyAH । tezAmaBAve sAmantA mOlavfdDodDftAdayaH । sTAvare zawprakAre'pi kAryyA nAtra vicAraReti kAtyAyanena kramaviDAnAt । ete ca sAmantAdayaH saMKyAguRAtirekena saMBavanti । “sAmantAH sADanaM pUrvvaMnirdozAH syurguRAnvitAH ॥” dviguRAstUttarA jYeyAstato'nye m: सीता f. (less correctly written शीता; cf. सीमन्, सीर) a furrow, the track or line of a ploughshare (also personified, and apparently once worshipped as a kind of goddess resembling Pomona; in RV. iv, 57, 6, Sītā is invoked as presiding over agriculture or the fruits of the earth; in VS. xii, 69-72, Sītā ‘the Furrow’ is again personified and addressed, four furrows being required to be drawn at the ceremony when the above stanzas are recited; in TBr. she is called सावित्री, and in PārGṛ. इन्द्र-पत्नी, ‘the wife of Indra’; in epic poetry S˚ is the wife of Rāmacandra and daughter of Janaka, king of Mithilā, capital of Videha, who was otherwise called Sīradhvaja; she was named Sītā because fabled to have sprung from a furrow made by Janaka while ploughing the ground to prepare it for a sacrifice instituted by him to obtain progeny, whence her epithet Ayoni-jā, ‘not womb-born’; her other common names, Maithilī and Vaidehī, are from the place of her birth; according to one legend she was Vedavatī q.v., in the Kṛta age; accord. to others she was an incarnation of Lakṣmi and of Umā; the story of Rāma's bending the bow, which was to be the condition of the gift of Sītā, is told in R. i, 67; Sītā's younger sister Urmilā was at the same time given to Lakṣmaṇa, and two nieces of Janaka, daughters of his brother king Kuśa-dhvaja, to Bharata and Śatrughna), RV. &c. &c., IW. 335 n. 1; 337 &c.

a: सीता — [सि-त पृषो˚ दीर्घः] 1 A furrow, track or line of a ploughshare. --2 (Hence) A tilled or furrowed ground, ploughed land; वृषेव सीतां तदवग्रहक्षतां Ku. 5. 61. --3 Husbandry, agriculture; as in सीताद्रव्य q. v. --4 N. of the daughter of Janaka, king of Mithilā, and wife of Rāma. [She was so called because she was supposed to have sprung from a furrow made by king Janaka while ploughing the ground to prepare it for a sacrifice which he had instituted to obtain progeny, and hence also her epithets, ‘Ayonijā’, ‘Dharāputrī’ &c. She was married to Rāma and accompanied him to the forest. While there she was once carried off by Rāvaṇa who tried to violate her chastity, but she scornfully rejected his suit. When Rāma came to know that she was in Laṅkā, he attacked the place, killed Rāvaṇa and his host of demons, and recovered Sītā. She had, however, to pass through the terrible ordeal of fire before she could be received by her husband as his wife. Though thus convinced of her chastity, he had afterwards to abandon her, when far advanced in pregnancy, because the people continued to suspect her fidelity. She, however, found a protector, in the sage Vālmīki, at whose hermitage she was delivered of Kuśa and Lava, and who brought them up. She was ultimately restored to Rāma by the sage.]. --5 N. of a goddess, wife of Indra. --6 N. of Umā. --7 N. of Lakṣmī. --8 N. of one of the fabulous branches of the Ganges. --9 Spirituous liquor. --Comp. --द्रव्यं implements of agriculture, tools of husbandry; Ms. 9. 293. --पतिः N. of Rāmachandra. --फलः the custard-apple tree. --(लं) its fruit.
